data.label: Display Unit
data.description: Touchscreen HMI connected to MCU via I2C/MIPI-DSI. Renders navigation, media, and system UI.

data.label: Audio Amplifier
data.description: Digital audio amplifier linked via I2S. Drives cabin speakers for media and navigation voice.

data.label: Bluetooth Module
data.description: BT 5.x / BLE module linked via HCI UART. Handles phone pairing, A2DP audio, HFP calls, PBAP contacts.

data.label: Wi-Fi Module
data.description: 802.11ac Wi-Fi connected via SDIO. Used for OTA updates, cloud API, and hotspot.

data.label: USB Interface
data.description: USB 2.0 host port (USB2). Supports CarPlay, Android Auto, media playback, and firmware flashing.

data.label: Microphone
data.description: Cabin microphone for voice commands and hands-free calls. Connects via ADC line-in.

data.label: Rear Camera Input
data.description: Rear-view camera video feed received via MIPI-CSI2. Rendered on display during reverse.

data.label: CAN Transceiver
data.description: CAN FD transceiver bridging the IVI MCU to the vehicle CAN bus for vehicle speed, warning signals.

data.label: User Profiles
data.description: PII data: driver preferences, paired device list, call/contact history, seat/mirror settings.

data.label: Navigation Data
data.description: GPS route history, saved POIs, destination logs. High-privacy sensitivity per ISO 21434.

data.label: Code Flash
data.description: IVI OS firmware (Linux/QNX) and application stack. Tamper causes compromised behaviour or bricking.

data.label: Data Flash
data.description: Non-volatile memory for calibration tables, variant coding, and persistent configuration.

data.label: Keys
data.description: TLS private key, OTA package signing verification key, Bluetooth link keys. Stored in secure element / HSM.

data.label: Certificates
data.description: X.509 TLS client certificate and secure boot certificate chain. Required for cloud and OTA authentication.

data.label: Debug Port
data.description: JTAG/UART debug interface. Must be disabled in production. Exposure enables full MCU memory read.

data.label: Vehicle CAN Bus
data.description: Vehicle-wide CAN FD backbone shared with other ECUs (BCM, ADAS, Cluster, etc.).

data.label: Smartphone
data.description: User's paired mobile device. Communicates over Bluetooth (HFP/A2DP/PBAP) and USB (CarPlay/Android Auto).

data.label: Cloud Backend
data.description: OEM cloud services: OTA update server, telematics API, map updates, remote diagnostics.

data.label: OBD-II Port
data.description: Physical diagnostic access port. Exposes UDS services on CAN. Must be access-controlled.

Details.Name: Malicious OTA Firmware Update via Wi-Fi
Details.Description: An attacker performs a man-in-the-middle attack over the Wi-Fi link (HTTPS channel) and injects a malicious firmware image into Code Flash. Because code signing verification (Certificates) is bypassed or the signing key (Keys) is compromised, the IVI MCU executes attacker-controlled firmware, enabling persistent access to the vehicle CAN bus and full cabin sensor control.

Details.Name: User PII Exfiltration via Bluetooth
Details.Description: An attacker exploits a Bluetooth pairing vulnerability (e.g., BIAS or KNOB attack) to impersonate a trusted device. By gaining authenticated HCI-level access, the attacker reads PBAP contact list, call history, and User Profiles stored in Data Flash, exfiltrating sensitive PII over the BT_Profile link to the attacker's device.

Details.Name: GPS Navigation Data Spoofing
Details.Description: An attacker injects falsified GPS NMEA sentences through an SDR-based GPS spoofer, causing Navigation Data stored in Data Flash to record fictitious routes. The manipulated navigation data misleads the driver to wrong or dangerous destinations. Per ISO 21434 Clause 15, this constitutes a loss of Authenticity and Integrity for location-based assets.

Details.Name: Malware Injection via USB Interface
Details.Description: A malicious USB device presents as a trusted CarPlay/Android Auto accessory. It exploits a USB stack parsing vulnerability (CWE-119) to overflow a buffer in the IVI OS running from Code Flash, achieving arbitrary code execution. The malware persists in Data Flash and may open a reverse tunnel to the CAN bus via the CAN Transceiver.

Details.Name: Microphone Eavesdropping (Cabin Audio Intercept)
Details.Description: A compromised IVI application or a software implant delivered via OTA continuously streams Microphone ADC input to a remote attacker over the Wi-Fi/HTTPS channel. The driver's private conversations, phone calls, and voice commands are captured without consent — a severe privacy violation under GDPR and ISO 21434 impact categories.

Details.Name: CAN Bus Injection via IVI Gateway
Details.Description: The IVI's CAN Transceiver is connected to the vehicle CAN bus shared with safety-critical ECUs (BCM, ADAS, Cluster). An attacker who has compromised IVI Code Flash injects spoofed CAN frames (e.g., fake wheel speed messages, door lock commands) onto the Vehicle CAN Bus. This can manipulate other ECU behaviour and compromise vehicle safety — directly violating SFOP Safety and Operational impact categories.

Details.Name: Debug Port Exploitation for Key Extraction
Details.Description: An attacker with physical access connects a JTAG debugger to the exposed Debug Port. With the debug interface active (or improperly locked), full MCU memory can be read, exposing Keys (TLS private keys, OTA signing keys, Bluetooth link keys) and Certificates stored in the secure element / HSM. This enables offline decryption of past sessions and forging of OTA packages.

Details.Name: Rear Camera Feed Substitution
Details.Description: An attacker injects a falsified MIPI-CSI2 video stream onto the Rear Camera Input using a hardware interposer or by exploiting an in-vehicle Ethernet/CSI bridge. The Display Unit shows a manipulated or frozen rear view during reversing, creating a dangerous blind spot. Loss of Integrity of the camera feed constitutes a Safety impact at Severe level.

Details.Name: Wi-Fi MITM — Cloud API Token Theft
Details.Description: An attacker sets up a rogue Wi-Fi access point with the same SSID as a known network. The IVI auto-connects and performs TLS certificate validation using stored Certificates; if certificate pinning is absent or Certificates are compromised, the attacker performs TLS termination and steals Cloud Backend API tokens and session credentials transmitted over HTTPS.

Details.Name: OBD-II Diagnostic Abuse — Unauthorised UDS Service Execution
Details.Description: An attacker connects to the physical OBD-II Port with a standard ELM327 adapter and issues UDS service 0x27 (Security Access) without a valid seed-key challenge. A weak or unprotected diagnostic session allows reading of Data Flash calibration tables, erasing diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), or invoking ECU reset commands — violating Integrity and Authorization of the CAN Transceiver and Data Flash assets.
